case.name: Severe-rainfall forecast explanations (explainability)
case.description: Illustrative example. A fictional data-driven weather model whose forecasts of heavy rainfall come with explanations for duty forecasters.

tree.name: G1
tree.description: The explanations shown with the forecast model's heavy-rainfall forecasts are fit for duty forecasters to use when deciding whether to issue a warning.

children.name: S1
children.description: Argument over three properties of the attribution maps' fidelity to the model: dependence on what the model learned, ranking first the input regions the forecast depends on, and agreement with how much the model relies on each input variable overall.

children.name: P1
children.description: Attribution maps made from the forecast model with its learned weights randomised have a structural similarity below 0.3 to the maps from the trained model.

children.name: E1
children.description: Sanity-check report SC-4.1, table 2: structural similarity between maps from the trained and weight-randomised model for 200 forecasts from the 2025 verification set. Covers model version 4.1; run by the model team; assumes the 200 forecasts represent the heavy-rainfall cases forecasters meet.

children.name: P2
children.description: The attribution maps rank first the input regions whose deletion changes the forecast at the selected location fastest, compared with a random ranking of the same regions.

children.name: E2
children.description: Deletion-curve analysis DC-4.1, figure 3: 500 heavy-rainfall forecasts from the 2025 verification set, compared with a random-removal baseline. Covers model version 4.1; run by the model team; assumes that replacing a region with its climate average removes its information.

children.name: P3
children.description: The input variables that the attribution maps rank highest on average are the ones whose shuffling most reduces the forecast model's skill on heavy-rainfall cases.

children.name: E3
children.description: Permutation-importance analysis PM-4.1, table 2: the drop in forecast skill on 500 heavy-rainfall cases from the 2025 verification set when each input variable is shuffled, set against each variable's average rank in the attribution maps. Covers model version 4.1; run by the model team; assumes the input variables are not strongly correlated.

children.justification: Each property rules out a different way an attribution map can look plausible without reflecting the model.

children.name: S2
children.description: Argument over three properties of the explanations in use: how well they convey the model's behaviour to forecasters, their effect on warning decisions, and their delivery time.

children.name: P4
children.description: The explanations let duty forecasters simulate the forecast model, predicting its output for new cases more accurately than they can without them.

children.name: P5
children.description: The explanations are useful to duty forecasters in cases where they disagree with the model.

children.name: E4
children.description: Reliance trial report RL-1, table 4: 24 duty forecasters deciding 60 past heavy-rainfall cases with and without the explanations, in random order. Covers model version 4.1; run by the service's human-factors team; assumes decisions in a trial match decisions on shift.

children.name: P6
children.description: The explanations reach the duty forecaster within 30 seconds of each forecast run, and score above the midpoint of a standard explanation-satisfaction scale among duty forecasters.

children.name: E5
children.description: Latency log LL-25, per-run records: time from each forecast run to its explanation reaching the forecaster's console, winter 2025–26. Covers the operational explanation service; logged automatically; assumes the console clocks are synchronised.

children.name: E6
children.description: Explanation-satisfaction survey ES-1, summary table: 40 duty forecasters rating the explanations on a standard eight-item scale. Covers model version 4.1; self-reported; assumes the respondents represent all duty forecasters.

children.justification: An explanation that is faithful but misread, ignored or late does not help the warning decision.

context: Use: duty forecasters at a national weather service see an explanation beside each heavy-rainfall forecast, as one input to the decision to issue a warning.
Heavy-rainfall forecast: a forecast of rainfall above the service's warning threshold at a location within the next 48 hours.
Explanation: an attribution map of which input variables and grid regions most influenced the forecast at a selected location, made with integrated gradients.
Fit for use: the explanations reflect what drove the forecast, and forecasters who use them make better warning decisions than forecasters who do not.
tree.justification: Confidence: medium. The evidence covers model version 4.1 and the 2025 verification set only.
